lines.text: In open world games, the cops are on you instantly. Real speed cameras are almost that quick, using pure physics.
Radar cameras fire radio waves at your car. The waves bounce back at a slightly different frequency.
That's the Doppler effect, why a siren sounds higher coming toward you. Bigger shift, faster car.
Laser guns, called lidar, fire short pulses of infrared light instead and time how long each takes to bounce back.
They take hundreds of distance readings in about a third of a second, and the change in distance gives your speed.
Their beam is so narrow it can pick out one car in traffic.
Some systems skip both: cameras read your plate at two points, and distance divided by time gives your average speed.
